html:
The Lake Miwok are a Miwok people of the land south of Clear Lake in northern California, around today's Lower Lake and Middletown. Their language is the most northern of the Miwok languages and borrowed many words from the Pomo and Wappo languages around it.

They lived in small villages, gathered acorns, fished in the lake and creeks, and hunted. Their land was a crossroads between the Pomo to the north and west, the Wappo to the south and the Patwin to the east.

After 1840 ranchers took their land and used Native people as forced labour. In 1850 US soldiers killed many Pomo at Bloody Island on Clear Lake, close by. Lake Miwok descendants live today at the Middletown Rancheria. See also Miwok.
